questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VII, Section 706, what are the TWO conditions that must be satisfied before a building may qualify for a floor area increase?

options.text: Installation of a full NFPA 13 sprinkler system AND approval of the Building Official, provided that the system covers all floors and areas
Public space, streets, or yards adjoining at least one side of the building AND Building Official approval, contingent upon compliance with local zoning ordinances
Public space, streets, or yards extending along and adjoining two or more sides of the building AND subject to Building Official approval
A corner lot location AND a minimum FLAR of 3.0, which must be verified by a licensed surveyor

questions.text: In the Philippine floor area framework under PD 1096, what does PSO (Percent of Site Occupancy) multiplied by TLA (Total Lot Area) produce?

options.text: Total Allowable GFA, which determines the maximum floor area that can be constructed on a given lot
AMBF (Allowable Maximum Building Footprint)
TGFA (Total Gross Floor Area), which includes all covered areas of a building
FLAR (Floor to Lot Area Ratio), a measure of density and land use efficiency

questions.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: AMBF = TLA × PSO is the foundational formula for determining the maximum building footprint. This is distinct from FLAR (which controls total floor area across all floors) and GFA (which is the actual computed floor area). The AMBF limits horizontal coverage; FLAR limits total building volume.

questions.text: Which of the following areas is EXCLUDED from the calculation of Gross Floor Area (GFA) under the 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096?

All corridors, lobbies, and toilets within the building envelope, as they are essential for circulation and services
Enclosed mezzanines, which are considered part of the usable floor space

PSO applies only to residential buildings; FLAR applies only to commercial buildings, a simplification that does not reflect actual regulations

The building must comply with Fire Restrictive Zone requirements because the majority of its floor area (1,150 sq m) is located in that zone, following the predominant-area rule

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Sec. 803, USA (Unpaved Surface Area) is specifically described in the IRR as what type of open space?

options.text: The 'permitted open space' — any outdoor area not covered by the building structure including driveways and paved courts
The 'true open space' — the portion that must remain unpaved with exposed soil and planting for ecological function
The 'required open space' — the minimum front setback distance mandated by the local zoning ordinance
The 'total open space' — all lot area not occupied by the enclosed building footprint including paved open areas

Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 803.3.b.ii explicitly describes USA as the 'true open space' — the portion of TLA that must remain unpaved with exposed soil and planting. It serves stormwater percolation, microclimate cooling, and groundwater recharge. Option A describes ISA (driveways, paved courts). Option C describes setback requirements, not USA. Option D describes TOSL (= ISA + USA), not USA alone.
questions.explanation: USA = 'true open space' per the IRR. TOSL = ISA + USA = all non-building open space (hard + soft). USA is the soft/permeable portion only. The distinction matters: a developer cannot satisfy the USA minimum with concrete pavers — it must be actual unpaved soil and planting.

questions.text: An architect calculates PSO for a Basic R-2 project and states: 'The PSO is 275 square meters.' A colleague responds: 'That is the AMBF, not the PSO.' Who is correct, and what is the proper statement of the PSO?

options.text: The architect is correct — PSO can be expressed in sq.m. for lots smaller than 500 sq.m. under Rule VIII conventions, which is a common practice
The colleague is correct — PSO is always expressed as a percentage; 275 sq.m. is the AMBF derived from PSO (55%) applied to a 500 sq.m. lot
Both are correct — PSO and AMBF are interchangeable terms for the same metric in Rule VIII, which is a misunderstanding
The colleague is partially correct — PSO can be in sq.m. for residential zones but must be in percent for commercial zones, which is a nuanced interpretation

AMBF is the area in sq.m. derived from applying PSO to TLA: AMBF = TLA x PSO = 500 x 0.55 = 275 sq.m. Calling 275 sq.m. the 'PSO' is a unit error — PSO = 55%, AMBF = 275 sq.m. Options A, C, and D all permit PSO to be expressed as an area, which violates the definitions in Sec. 803. This is Trap 4 from the area metrics article.
questions.explanation: PSO = percentage (e.g., 55%). AMBF = area in sq.m. = TLA x PSO. Mnemonic: 'MACA is more than just the building; AMBF is the actual building footprint.' Mixing units (calling 275 sq.m. the PSO) is a conceptual error that triggers wrong calculations in multi-step problems. Always state PSO as a percent and AMBF as an area.
